name: rooftop-pirate-transmission
style: Sunday-night jungle pirate broadcast, 1994, sent from a homemade transmitter on the roof of a 21-storey council tower and caught on a cheap kitchen radio. 165 BPM instrumental. The drums lead the whole way: the Amen chopped into stuttering fragments, re-edited, doubled up, rolling relentlessly, crash cymbals smashed hard over to the left. Beneath it, a reversed sub-bass that inhales backwards into every downbeat and lands as a deep concrete boom, the Renegade trick of 1994. The space between sub and cymbals stays empty. The only other sound is the radio itself: FM hiss, the signal drifting off-station and snapping back, a faint mono wobble. Bare, cold, raw, unmelodic, all rhythm and sub. Starts mid-set, already at full tilt, and loops seamlessly.
exclude: voice, lyrics, toasting, shout-outs, ragga, reggae, Reese bass, midrange bassline, synth lead, rave stabs, pads, strings, piano, riser, build-up, intro
